newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile June retail sales rise five percent.
newsitem.headline: Chile June retail sales rise five percent.

text.p: Chilean retail sales grew five percent in June from a year earlier, bringing the increase in the first six months of the year to 3.1 percent, the National Chamber of Commerce said Tuesday.
Alfonso Mujica, president of the chamber, said retail sales growth in the first half was much slower than in the first six months of 1996, when sales increased 7.4 percent.
Industries reporting the stongest retail sales growth in the January-June period included footware, up 20 percent, and clothing, up 13 percent.
"In both cases, the rise is explained by heavy sales carried out to overcome the impact of the (economic) adjustment and as a result of imports of cheaper foreign products," said Mujica.
The chamber expects retail sales growth to pick up sharply in the second half, to 7.4 percent, as a result of the Central Bank's recent interest rate cuts, he said.
The improvement in sales forecast in coming months should boost retail sales growth to around 5.5 percent for 1997 as a whole, he said.
